summary: Read-only cadence entrypoint (`make worktree-sweep` / `worktree-sweep-apply`) plus runbook for keeping git worktrees from accumulating; classification and removal live in scripts/worktree-cleanup.sh, not in the Makefile itself.

entry_points.summary: Read-only: runs worktree-cleanup.sh classify and prints per-bucket counts. Never removes anything.
Dry-run: prints the exact `worktree-cleanup.sh remove <path>` command per safe-remove worktree. Prints only, never executes.

invariants: make worktree-sweep never removes anything by itself.
make worktree-sweep-apply only prints remove commands; it never executes them.
Actual removal always goes through scripts/worktree-cleanup.sh remove (or after-merge), which refuses dirty/unmerged worktrees without --force.
Run the sweep from the MAIN tree, never from inside a linked worktree.
gotchas: A single repo's worktrees can live under three different parent directories (in-repo .claude/worktrees/, external ../<repo>-worktrees/, and ~/.hermes/worktrees/...); `git worktree list` (which the classifier uses) already covers all three in one call, so no per-location sweep is needed.

worktree-cleanup.sh classify exits non-zero style failures are not distinguished per-bucket in the Makefile output beyond the four bucket names (safe-remove/merged-dirty/unmerged-work/dead-pointer); see scripts/worktree-cleanup.sh for the full JSON schema.
